newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PROTESTER KILLED IN SKIRMISH WITH S.AFRICAN POLICE.
newsitem.headline: PROTESTER KILLED IN SKIRMISH WITH S.AFRICAN POLICE.

text.p: A protester aligned to a militant anti-drug Moslem movement was killed in skirmishes with police at one of South Africa's premier tourist meccas on Sunday, eyewitnesses and hospital staff reported.
"One person was dead on arrival and we're treating four people with minor injuries," an official from Cape Town's Somerset Hospital told Reuters.

Scores more were hurt in clashes at the Victoria and Alfred Waterfront, including a woman who was shot in the neck. Her husband vowed retribution, telling reporters: "For the blood of my wife, I will get blood from them."
The People Against Gangerism and Drugs (Pagad) group burst into the limelight in August when its members publicly shot and burned to death an alleged drug merchant and gang leader near Cape Town.
Police could not immediately confirm the man's death, nor the number of those injured, but said they would investigate.
Captain Wicus Holtzhausen said policemen, heavily armed and in full riot gear, had intervened when the crowd had ignored a warning to disperse.
"Police started arresting them. That was when they started throwing bottles and then the police fired rubber bullets," he said.
Many demonstrators were searched and disarmed at a police roadblock leading to the Waterfront, a popular shopping and entertainment centre thronging with tourists.
Pagad members gained entrance to the main building by kicking down glass doors. Another group rained missiles including bottles and chairs onto police from a first floor balcony.
Demonstrators also took plates of food from outdoor diners to hurl at police.
In the ensuing chaos shoppers and restaurant patrons rushed for shelter, locking themselves behind glass doors for safety.
Shattered window-fronts, broken bottles and empty rubber bullet cartridges bore testimony to the clash as the area emptied.

Last month, 28 people were hurt when police used rubber bullets and birdshot to disperse a crowd which tossed stones at policemen in a demonstration against drug dealers at Clanwilliam, about 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Cape Town.
Crowds of vigilantes threatening to kill drug barons who do not give up their trade have repeatedly confronted police during marches to the homes of alleged dealers around South Africa.
